question: Do the KG-grounded and CG-grounded supervision arms use the identical QA items and questions, differing only in the attached evidence, or do they differ in question content and difficulty as well?
description: The comparison between KG-grounded and CG-grounded supervision assumes the two datasets differ only in evidence type. If the CG-grounded QA items are different questions (for example generated from context-dependent paths, or regenerated with the context graph, or filtered differently), then question distribution and difficulty differ across arms in addition to supervision volume, and the CG-over-KG gap would confound supervision format with item content. The closest work's text found so far does not state that the identical question set is used across the two regimes, and the full dataset statistics were not located.
rationale: If questions differ across arms, the central comparison has a second confound beyond volume, and the re-run must fix the question set to make the contrast interpretable; this is cheap to check in the paper's dataset section and appendix and would be enforced by design in experiment E001.
